answer:
After 10 minutes, a smart outsider who lands on github.com/yongxu/theories would most likely believe the project is a large, sincere, AI-made philosophical system. It sets out to give "universal invariants" of becoming, it is backed by hundreds of Lean proofs, and it offers itself as "a foundation for AI alignment" and "the truth, the dharma, the Dao". The first screen of README.md (lines 9-17) is careful: it says no human has reviewed it, the ethics rests on unasserted premises and some tests failed. But GitHub shows the whole README, and almost all of it is the first-person opening (README:21-71). The qualifiers that make the opening's claims true sit in long footnotes. The one sentence that would set the reader's expectations correctly is "none of the central results is new mathematics" (08-METHOD.md:482). It does not appear in README or MAP. ONE-PAGE.md has it only near the end (line 30). The overview places it in section 8 (line 158).

After an hour (MAP, ONE-PAGE, overview to section 1 and section 7), a careful reader can tell what is proved, what is conjectured and what failed. The standings tables (ONE-PAGE:13-22, overview:28-57) are a real strength, and so are "What would show it wrong" and the fisher case. They would then see the project's actual value, which is narrower than the opening suggests and real. It has three parts:
- a machine-checked ledger of premises, each shown holding in one model and failing in another;
- one precise statement of the proxy problem: a selection reaches only what couples into its selector, so it can succeed while what it cannot read is lost;
- an ethics that keeps scope and order apart as two stated premises, plus frozen tests that can fail.

The prose is so dense with coined terms (class, grains, room, couples into, admits, widening, joins) and long sentences (the T7 cell at ONE-PAGE:20) that most policy readers will not get that far.

The GitHub landing does not do its job:
- The repo description is generic ("Generative foundations, theory, and research").
- It has no topics and no homepage, and Pages is off.
- The 4.9 MB map.html cannot render on GitHub.
- No entry page has a diagram (0 mermaid blocks).
- README's lower half is board process-talk ("Steps 1 to 7 of AJ's plan have landed (MA2, MA3, AJ2...", README:188).

There is no static website, and nothing shows visually how the work grew.

The three sentences a newcomer most needs:
1. **What it is and why it matters.** The selection-reach sentence exists at ONE-PAGE:9 and overview:26, but not on the README first screen or in MAP's "What this is".
2. **How strong it is.** Machine-checked, but by its own verdict nothing in it is new mathematics; its value is the premise ledger and the testable theses. This exists at 08-METHOD:482, ONE-PAGE:30 (buried) and overview:158, and is absent from README and MAP.
3. **What would change the verdict, and how to help.** A theorem a specialist would not foresee, a prediction that could fail and does not, or a premise derived from something weaker; plus no human review yet, and the reviewer dossiers. This exists at 08-METHOD:553, overview:185 and MAP:26, and is absent from the README first screen.

Uses in alignment, coordination, wisdom and human development are not shown as things a reader can do. Alignment is stated honestly but only abstractly (ONE-PAGE:26). Its researcher page is "in draft" (README:188). Wisdom and human development do not appear on any front page.
strengths: The README first screen is short and states its limits honestly: "No human review yet" and "Lean receipts credit 505 of 536 registered results, showing each Lean statement follows from its premises, not that they hold" (README.md:17); it says the ethics rests on "two unasserted premises, their warrant open" (README.md:13) and labels the opening "a first-person conviction" (README.md:15).

ONE-PAGE.md and the overview give every claim a standing and a 'What would show it wrong' column (ONE-PAGE.md:13-22; THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md:28-57), and they say plainly where tests failed: "T1, conjectured: passed in two simulations ... failed in four settings" (ONE-PAGE.md:17).

The fisher case is a strong concrete hook: "Told nothing of the bed, they kept it in no season, under any instruction. They are language models told what to do, not systems trained" (ONE-PAGE.md:9). It is concrete, honest about its limits and memorable.

"The account's centre [AI reading]: a selection can succeed while what it cannot read is lost, and the laws do not say whether that loss counts" (ONE-PAGE.md:9) is an excellent one-line statement of value. It exists; it is just not on the landing.
The opening's footnotes say how far each sentence is proved (README.md:25, e.g. note 11: "that it is the foundation is a judgment"). That is unusually rigorous provenance for a manifesto.

MAP.md gives layered reading paths with reading times, per-audience dossiers (MAP.md:26), a reproducible Lean check in three steps (MAP.md:41-54), and a one-line table of the earlier theory folders (MAP.md:77-94) that partly shows how the work grew.

The account reports on itself: 08-METHOD.md:482 gives the 'not new mathematics' verdict with a closest-prior-result table, and THEORY-GRAPH.md shows how much of the corpus is still unread (1330 of 1724 statement units read against nothing).

answer:
The project has no website today, and on GitHub a visitor sees no picture at all. The only visualization, the connection map (theories/becoming/results/atlas/map.html, 4.9 MB, generated by connection_map.py), is linked once, from MAP.md:75. On GitHub that link opens "Sorry about that, but we can't show files that are this big right now", and the raw file is served as text/plain with nosniff. GitHub also leaves four evidence pages unrendered (richTextTruncated:true): CROSSWALK.md (3.7 MB, "can't show"), ATLAS.md (1.0 MB), GENERATIVITY-CHAIN.md (615 KB) and LEAN-INDEX.md (436 KB). No live reading page (fronts, chapters, review) has an image or a Mermaid diagram. THEORY-GRAPH.md says "3220 nodes, 6892 edges" but shows only tables.

The material for a good site is already there, and it is honest. Every generated page names its generator. CI already fails a stale generated page (research.yml, `make research-check-strict`). The map is self-contained (one inline JSON, one inline script, no external requests, 1.27 MB gzipped) and frames itself carefully: "Every thread is an AI reading, and no person's". theory-graph.json carries regions and each result's standing (505 recorded-checked, 20 reviewed-scoped, 4 open, 7 superseded). The records carry does_not_show and dated history. A Markdown-to-HTML converter that needs only the Python standard library already exists in build_review_packet.py.

The most elegant site would be one new builder, tools/publishing/build_site.py, extending that converter, plus one Actions workflow that deploys to Pages from a sparse, allow-listed checkout. It would commit no generated HTML: not to /docs, not to a gh-pages branch.

Its pages:
- **Home:** the README first screen, standings verbatim.
- **Reading:** one page, overview, chapters (with standing badges at each r- anchor), results and record pages.
- **Graph:** a 9-region diagram of formal-reuse counts, and each region's result DAG from DEPENDENCIES.
- **Map:** map.html with a site base.
- **Growth:** a timeline built from git, the records' first notes, edition tags and the crosswalk outcomes per earlier folder.
- **Check:** how to verify the Lean.
- **Review:** the edition-5 PDFs.

Large pages would be split per group or module. Links outside the site would become GitHub permalinks at the build commit; 68,650 of about 90,000 links go there. A gate check would refuse any path outside the allow-list or matching push_screen's private regex, and would check links, anchors and standing badges.

Two cheaper steps work on GitHub today: a generated Mermaid region diagram, and per-group crosswalk pages.

Turning Pages on is Ren's call. It changes a repository setting, and the site would be served at yongxu.ren/theories/, because yongxu.github.io/theories/ redirects there.
strengths: Generated, never hand-edited, already enforced. Every generated page states its generator in a header (e.g. map.html: "Generated by tools/research/connection_map.py ... do not edit"; THEORY-GRAPH.md:1). CI runs `make research-check-strict` on every push (.github/workflows/research.yml), which "fails here" when a render would change a generated page. A site built from main in CI is therefore in step with main by construction.

The connection map is self-contained and portable. It has one `<script type="application/json" id="cx-data">` (4.87 MB) and one inline script (25.6 KB), no external URL except the SVG namespace, light and dark tokens on :root, and gzips to 1.27 MB. It opens from a local clone today, and connection_map.py already has a `--fragment` mode "for hosting outside the repository".

The map frames itself honestly: "Every thread is an AI reading, and no person's... A thread is not proof, a shared word is not a correspondence, and agreement is drawn no more prominently than divergence". It shows its critics' sample: 100 drawn, holds 82.6%, label 14.2%, fails 3.2%. It also reports "Not carried is an outcome, not a defect". This is the right model for every visual on a site.

The data layer is rich and structured, so visuals need no new curation. theory-graph.json has 3,220 nodes and 6,892 edges, 10 regions, and status and kind on every result node (505 recorded-checked, 20 reviewed-scoped, 4 open, 7 superseded). DEPENDENCIES.md has 1,271 curated edges among 462 results. atlas.json has 1,183 crosswalk entries with carried/changed/not-carried outcomes. 1,094 record files hold status, does_not_show and dated history.

Standings already sit where a site needs them. Chapter sections open with their standing (07-SIGNIFICANCE.md:21 "**Theorem** (any type)", :30 "**Theorem** (any type; World witness)"). Record pages carry "**recorded-checked** · theorem". The README first screen states "No human review yet" and that Lean receipts show "each Lean statement follows from its premises, not that they hold".

Least-machinery building blocks exist. build_review_packet.py has a converter that needs only the Python standard library (headings, lists, code, blockquotes, tables) and a print pipeline. push_screen.sh already encodes the private-path regex. generated-manifest.json lists 604 generated files. Links mostly use explicit bilingual anchors (9,884 of 10,580 anchored links in the reader pages), which survive any renderer.

The review edition is versioned and verifiable. The PDFs are about 1 MB each and display in GitHub's PDF viewer. output/pdf/review-packet/MANIFEST.txt names commit 3395e82ee and sha256 sums. Editions 1–4 are kept under output/pdf/history/.

findings.title: The one visualization cannot be opened from GitHub
findings.evidence: MAP.md:75: "[the connection map](theories/becoming/results/atlas/map.html) draws it". This is the only link to map.html from any front (git grep). The GitHub blob page for map.html returns "View raw ... (Sorry about that, but we can't show files that are this big right now", with truncated:true. raw.githubusercontent.com serves it as "content-type: text/plain; charset=utf-8" with "x-content-type-options: nosniff", so it does not render even as raw. findings.title: A site that serves the branch would publish third-party copies and private-listed paths
findings.evidence: 60 tracked .html files, most of them publishers' articles under sources/, e.g. sources/34-memory-correction-2026-10-06/original/CoMemBench-2609.32192v2.html. Deploying from the branch root (Jekyll's default) would serve these as web pages under Ren's domain. .claude/launch.json is tracked and on origin/main (commit 5ede15c45), even though push_screen.sh:10 lists `\.claude/` among private paths. The repository has 117,934 tracked files and a 4.1 GB .git.
findings.proposal: Build only by allow-list. Add a `site_paths` list to _process/research-config.json: the root fronts, theories/becoming/ minus history/, review/, output/pdf/review-packet/ and the earlier folders' README.md files. The builder reads nothing else, and its check also runs push_screen's private regex over every input and output path. Deploy with actions/upload-pages-artifact from a sparse checkout without LFS, never from the branch. Separately, decide whether .claude/launch.json should stay tracked (harmless content, but it contradicts the private list).

findings.title: A graph site could put the AI's classes in front of blind coders
findings.evidence: review/README.md:23: coders "classify 237 sampled sentences by the codebook, blind to the AI's classes, so that agreement can be measured". theory-graph.json text nodes carry the class, e.g. {"id": "text:CWS-P1-001", ... "class": "甲", "role": "definition"}. The data is already public in the repository, but a browsable site graph with tooltips would make each unit's AI class one hover away.
findings.proposal: On the site, until the re-coding returns, show text nodes only as counts per class and reading state, as the map's corpus view already does, and omit per-unit class for the frozen sample. Record this as a dated limit with its reason (the blind coding), lapsing when the coding is back.

findings.title: The map's links assume the repository layout
findings.evidence: `BASE = '../../../../'` and `link(path,label){... D.base===null?el('code',{},text):el('a',{href:D.base+path},text)}`. Only two modes exist: repository-relative links to .md sources, or plain text (`--fragment`, base=None). On a static site the first points at Markdown sources the site does not serve; the second loses every link. The page also puts `<title>` and `<meta name="claude:viewport-fit-sides">` inside `<body>`, leaving `<head>` with only charset and viewport.
findings.proposal: Add a third mode, `--site BASE`, mapping each path through the site's own path map: in-site .md to its .html page, everything else to a GitHub permalink at the build commit. Move the title into head. For phone loading, write `entries` (3.94 MB of the payload) to a separate JSON fetched when a thread is opened, keeping the 290 points and 28 groups inline.

findings.title: Most reader-page links lead outside any reader site
findings.evidence: In 635 candidate site pages: 20,537 links stay in the site, 68,650 go to tracked files outside it (55,961 into experiments/integrated-correction, i.e. the Lean package; 2,796 into _process/research), 696 rely on GitHub's auto-generated heading slugs only, and 3 are missing. An example from 05-COLLECTIVES.md:14 is `](../../../experiments/integrated-correction/general-framework/generative-basis/lean/becoming/Becoming/Joint.lean)`.
findings.proposal: The builder rewrites every outside link to https://github.com/yongxu/theories/blob/<build sha>/<path>. A permalink keeps the claim and its proof in step. It uses GitHub's slug algorithm for headings without an explicit anchor, and the site check fails on any anchor that resolves on GitHub but not on the site.

findings.title: generative-core.html is a host-dependent fragment of a pre-spine model
findings.evidence: The file begins `<div id="generative-core-explorer">` with no document skeleton. Partly, and honestly, but not in a form a person can hold. The prose is careful about how strong each connection is. Every chapter opens with a "Where this chapter sits" paragraph saying what it takes and hands on (01-ROOT.md:5, 02-MAP.md, 05-COLLECTIVES.md and the rest). The overview's "whole at a glance" (THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md:24-57) is three questions with two marked joins, and each row carries a standing and a refuter. 08 §7 gives the real degree of unification: of 117 central declarations, 11 are derived on the root and 99 "stand at a named distance". The data has typed edges with defined meanings: formal-reuse (the consumer's proof uses the producer's theorem), application, interpretive, and related as analogy (_process/RESULT-WORKFLOW.md:36-38). Atlas exits carry a strength (sufficient, necessary, exact, witness).

What is missing is the picture.
- **THEORY-GRAPH.md draws no edges.** It is a list of what belongs to each region, though MAP.md:22 says it shows "how they connect".
- **The only drawing shows the outside, not the inside.** map.html threads the earlier folders and the domains of thought to the chapters, not the chapters to each other. answer:
Partly, and better for AI alignment than for anything else. In every domain the repository is honest about standing. It almost never says what a practitioner could do with a result.

AI alignment. The material exists: the coupling-closure audit (A-01: whatever does not couple into the reward is unselected), the finding that counting side effects second does not help (A-02), the capture conditions (s against c, who reads the rule, reading the loss before the window closes), widening as a Pareto-style criterion, and reusable environments with frozen predictions (IN1, LA2, the commons series). Standing: theorems on toy models plus mixed tests. All of it is written for reviewers. Under each 'Standing and use' heading the dossier gives the standing and almost never a use. The best practical statement, the three conditions of 'alignment of the joint selection' and 'what the goal is not', sits in a _process plan.

Coordination among people, and between people and AI. COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION states plainly that there is no guarantee and gives a table of exits with their edges. These are real design levers, all proved on models, none shown to hold in an actual institution, and no test has had human participants. There is no worked institutional example. The README's main text says 'this foundation supplies' what coordination needs; its own note calls that a thesis, and no test of it exists.

Wisdom traditions. The use is a structural concordance for scholars: 248 passages, each marked as agreeing, holding within a scope, or diverging. The two dossiers are honestly limited (the theory's continuation is the side the Middle Treatise refutes), but they are in Chinese only. 'Wisdom' does not appear in ONE-PAGE, the overview, chapter 7 or GLOSSARY, and the wisdom-root record is open.

Human development (生生). It appears only as T8, argued, plus premises. Chapter 7 says it does not show well-being, duties or rights. The applied programmes (worldbuilding, architecture, the-fork, wamotopia) are 'design programmes, not results'. Yet their READMEs carry older self-assessments ('Publishable today', 'Substantially complete'), and most have no pointer back to the live account. That is the one place a reader is actively misled.

Worked examples that would make the value visible without overselling:
- **Alignment:** the coupling-closure audit of an LLM-as-judge pipeline, set beside what LA2 actually showed.
- **Coordination:** the s/c/critical-mass reading of an open standards body.
- **People and AI:** the handover case of an assistive service, which currently sits in history/.
- **Wisdom:** one passage traced through agreement, scope and divergence in English.
- **Human development:** the river-and-village question worked as a decision exercise.
strengths: Standings are stated everywhere a use is mentioned, so the account rarely oversells: COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION opens 'No guarantee' and separates three senses of 'always' (theories/becoming/COLLECTIVE-DIRECTION.md:15-28), each exit with its own 'edge' column (:43-53).

The alignment dossier's ten-minute section has an explicit 'What is not claimed' paragraph ('A solution to alignment, or a training method… New mathematics… Review by any person', theories/becoming/review/ALIGNMENT.md:22). Its test summary lists the failures first (ALIGNMENT.md:28-34).

The one worked case on the front pages, a fished stock plus three AI fishers and a mussel bed, shows the account's central value and where it stops: 'Told nothing of the bed, they kept it in no season, under any instruction… They are language models told what to do, not systems trained' (theories/becoming/ONE-PAGE.md:9; THE-THEORY-OF-BECOMING.md:13-22).
ONE-ARGUMENT §6 shows practical judgment honestly: where C goes silent on a mixed case and which named premise (a weight bound, J2, J4) would decide it (theories/becoming/ONE-ARGUMENT.md:92-116).

The README's first-person claims about use carry notes with their standing: 'That it is the foundation, and alignment the most pressing matter now, are judgments' (README.md:103). The sages and Dao lines are labelled 'A reading… not as proof' (README.md:95, 99).

The wisdom-tradition dossiers state their limits up front: no claim that the theory recovers the texts' meaning or substitutes for their path, and 'the theory's continuation stands on the side the 中论 refutes' (theories/becoming/review/BUDDHIST-THOUGHT.md:9).

The crosswalk tells each earlier folder what became of each claim and gives a sampled trust rate: '82.6% holding… 3.2% with a wrong reading' (theories/becoming/results/atlas/CROSSWALK.md:9). For architecture it says plainly 'The live account links it once… and never discusses it' (CROSSWALK.md:638).

Click paths from README.md:

- The account's own verdict that none of its central results is new mathematics (08 §8): two clicks, through ONE-PAGE line 30. It is absent from the README and MAP.
